source_text:
Hecks.bluebook "EmbryonautFoundersApp", version: "v1" do
  formerly_known_as "Embryonaut"

  vision "Our own company, run the way we ask our clients to run theirs — Members holding the cap table, governing documents carried to execution, clients proposed to and contracted with, products carried from a vision statement to launch, and the accounting that keeps it all honest: invoices raised, payments recorded."
  core

  aggregate "Member" do
    description "A person who holds Units in the Company under the Operating Agreement — Chris, Angie, Meredith today. Email is this Member's own identity — see Email's own comment for why. role/identity_id are app access, granted separately from admission (GrantAccess, below): equity and app access happen to coincide for everyone here today, but the language doesn't conflate them."

    identified_by :email

    attribute :email,               Email
    attribute :name,                MemberName
    attribute :title,               MemberTitle
    attribute :units,               Units
    attribute :percentage_interest, PercentageInterest
    attribute :vesting,             VestingSchedule
    attribute :role,                Role,       optional: true
    attribute :identity_id,         IdentityId, optional: true
    attribute :revisions,           list_of(Revision)

    value_object "MemberName" do
      attribute :value, String
      invariant("a Member is named") { !value.to_s.empty? }
    end

    value_object "MemberTitle" do
      attribute :value, String
      invariant("a Member holds a title") { !value.to_s.empty? }
    end

    value_object "Units" do
      attribute :count, Integer, default: 0
      invariant("Units are not negative") { !count.negative? }
    end

    value_object "PercentageInterest" do
      attribute :value, Float
      invariant("a Percentage Interest is at least 0")   { value >= 0 }
      invariant("a Percentage Interest is at most 100")  { value <= 100 }
    end

    # THE 4-YEAR / 1-YEAR-CLIFF SHAPE Article 7 spells out — a quarter at
    # the cliff, the rest in equal monthly installments after.
    value_object "VestingSchedule" do
      attribute :cliff_units,          Integer
      attribute :monthly_units,        Integer
      attribute :commencement_date,    String

      invariant("cliff Units are not negative")   { !cliff_units.negative? }
      invariant("monthly Units are not negative") { !monthly_units.negative? }
      invariant("vesting names its commencement date") { !commencement_date.to_s.empty? }
    end

    value_object "Email" do
      attribute :value, String
      invariant("an email is present") { !value.to_s.empty? }
    end

    # THE CLOSED SET — Admin/Member, nothing else. Governance itself
    # stays generic (it records whatever role_name string a domain
    # assigns, since Banking's own roles look nothing like these); this
    # is the one place in the language a closed set CAN live — a
    # one_of only holds inside the chapter that declares it, so app
    # access roles have to be validated here, on Embryonaut's own
    # aggregate, not on Governance::RoleAssignment itself. "Member" as
    # a role value (app access level) and "Member" as this aggregate's
    # own name are two different things that happen to share a word —
    # a cap-table Member and someone with the "Member" access role are
    # usually the same person here, but the language doesn't conflate
    # them.
    value_object "Role" do
      attribute :value, String, one_of: ["Admin", "Member"]
    end

    # SAME SHAPE AS Governance::RoleAssignment's OWN IdentityId and
    # Identity::ExternalIdentifier's — a local duplicate, correlated by
    # matching string value rather than a real cross-chapter reference,
    # the established way this codebase already crosses that boundary.
    value_object "IdentityId" do
      attribute :value, String
      invariant("an identity id is present") { !value.to_s.empty? }
    end

    value_object "Revision" do
      attribute :sequence, Integer
      attribute :summary,  String

      invariant("a revision is sequenced from one") { sequence.positive? }
      invariant("a revision says what changed") { !summary.to_s.empty? }
    end

    lifecycle :status, default: "active" do
      transition "Depart" => "departed", from: "active"
    end

    command "Admit" do
      role "Managing Member"
      goal "Bring a new Member onto the cap table"

      attribute :email,               Email
      attribute :name,                MemberName
      attribute :title,               MemberTitle
      attribute :units,               Units
      attribute :percentage_interest, PercentageInterest
      attribute :vesting,             VestingSchedule

      sets :email
      sets :name
      sets :title
      sets :units
      sets :percentage_interest
      sets :vesting

      emits "MemberAdmitted"
    end

    command "Depart" do
      role "Managing Member"
      goal "Record that a Member has left — Units go to repurchase, not deletion"

      reference_to Member

      emits "MemberDeparted"
    end

    # APP ACCESS, GRANTED SEPARATELY FROM ADMISSION — every Member
    # already has an email (it's their own identity, set at Admit), so
    # this only needs to grant a role, not restate it. Gated to "Admin"
    # at both the app layer (Ports::Authorization.holds_role?,
    # Governance-backed) and here, at the command's own declared role —
    # see web/app.rb's /admin/users route.
    command "GrantAccess" do
      role "Admin"
      goal "Let an existing Member sign in to this application"

      reference_to Member
      attribute :role, Role

      sets :role

      emits "MemberAccessGranted"
    end

    # DISPATCHED BY THE APP ITSELF the moment a person's first real
    # Google sign-in mints their Identity (see embryonaut_console's
    # Auth.auto_provision) — role "System", the same convention
    # ScheduledPayment.Fail/Retry use elsewhere for app-triggered,
    # not human-triggered, dispatches.
    command "LinkIdentity" do
      role "System"
      goal "Attach the real Identity a person's first Google sign-in minted"

      reference_to Member
      attribute :identity_id, IdentityId

      sets :identity_id

      emits "MemberIdentityLinked"
    end

    command "Revise" do
      role "Managing Member"
      goal "Log a change to a Member's own record — the same revision history a real cap table amendment tracks"

      reference_to Member
      attribute :sequence, Integer
      attribute :summary,  String

      sets :revisions, append: { sequence: :sequence, summary: :summary }

      emits "MemberRevised"
    end

    query "Active" do
      description "The current cap table."
      where(status: "active")
      order_by :name
    end

    # email IS this aggregate's own identity now (see identified_by
    # above), so "the Member with this email" is a plain id lookup —
    # no ByEmail query needed. identity_id is NOT the primary key
    # though, so finding a Member by it still needs a real query.
    query "ByIdentityId" do
      description "The Member row for a real, already-linked Identity."
      attribute :identity_id, IdentityId
      where(identity_id: :identity_id)
    end
  end

  aggregate "FoundingAgreement" do
    description "A governing document among the Members — the Operating Agreement, the IP Assignment Agreement, or the Hecks/Embryonaut Boundary — carried from draft to full execution."

    identified_by :reference

    attribute :reference,   AgreementReference
    attribute :title,       AgreementTitle
    attribute :kind,        one_of("OperatingAgreement", "IPAssignment", "Boundary")
    attribute :version,     AgreementVersion
    attribute :signatories, list_of(Signatory)
    attribute :revisions,   list_of(Revision)

    value_object "AgreementReference" do
      attribute :value, String
      invariant("an agreement is referenced") { !value.to_s.empty? }
    end

    value_object "AgreementTitle" do
      attribute :value, String
      invariant("an agreement is titled") { !value.to_s.empty? }
    end

    value_object "AgreementVersion" do
      attribute :value, String
      invariant("an agreement carries a version") { !value.to_s.empty? }
    end

    value_object "Signatory" do
      attribute :name, String
      invariant("a signatory is named") { !name.to_s.empty? }
    end

    value_object "Revision" do
      attribute :sequence, Integer
      attribute :summary,  String

      invariant("a revision is sequenced from one") { sequence.positive? }
      invariant("a revision says what changed") { !summary.to_s.empty? }
    end

    lifecycle :status, default: "drafted" do
      transition "Circulate" => "circulated", from: "drafted"
      transition "Execute"   => "executed",   from: "circulated"
      transition "Withdraw"  => "withdrawn",  from: ["drafted", "circulated"]
    end

    command "Draft" do
      role "Managing Member"
      goal "Put a governing document in writing, for attorney review"

      attribute :reference, AgreementReference
      attribute :title,     AgreementTitle
      attribute :kind,      one_of("OperatingAgreement", "IPAssignment", "Boundary")
      attribute :version,   AgreementVersion

      sets :reference
      sets :title
      sets :kind
      sets :version

      emits "FoundingAgreementDrafted"
    end

    command "Circulate" do
      role "Managing Member"
      goal "Send the draft to every Member for signature"

      reference_to FoundingAgreement

      emits "FoundingAgreementCirculated"
    end

    command "Execute" do
      role "Managing Member"
      goal "Record that every Member has signed"

      reference_to FoundingAgreement
      attribute :signatories, list_of(Signatory)

      sets :signatories

      emits "FoundingAgreementExecuted"
    end

    command "Withdraw" do
      role "Managing Member"
      goal "Pull a draft governing document that will never be executed"

      reference_to FoundingAgreement

      emits "FoundingAgreementWithdrawn"
    end

    command "Revise" do
      role "Managing Member"
      goal "Log a change to a governing document's own draft — the same revision history a real client folder tracks"

      reference_to FoundingAgreement
      attribute :sequence, Integer
      attribute :summary,  String

      sets :revisions, append: { sequence: :sequence, summary: :summary }

      emits "FoundingAgreementRevised"
    end

    query "Executed" do
      description "Governing documents fully in force."
      where(status: "executed")
    end
  end

  aggregate "Client" do
    description "A company or person we sell to. Churned rather than deleted — we forget nothing about who we've worked with."

    identified_by :reference

    attribute :reference,      ClientReference
    attribute :name,           ClientName
    attribute :contact_email,  EmailAddress
    attribute :revisions,      list_of(Revision)

    value_object "ClientReference" do
      attribute :value, String
      invariant("a client is referenced") { !value.to_s.empty? }
    end

    value_object "ClientName" do
      attribute :value, String
      invariant("a client is named") { !value.to_s.empty? }
    end

    value_object "EmailAddress" do
      attribute :address, String, pattern: '^[^@ ]+@[^@ ]+\.[^@ ]+$'
    end

    value_object "Revision" do
      attribute :sequence, Integer
      attribute :summary,  String

      invariant("a revision is sequenced from one") { sequence.positive? }
      invariant("a revision says what changed") { !summary.to_s.empty? }
    end

    lifecycle :status, default: "prospect" do
      transition "Engage"     => "active",   from: "prospect"
      transition "Pause"      => "dormant",  from: "active"
      transition "Reactivate" => "active",   from: ["dormant", "churned"]
      transition "Churn"      => "churned",  from: ["active", "dormant"]
    end

    command "AddProspect" do
      role "COO"
      goal "Bring a prospect into the pipeline"

      attribute :reference,     ClientReference
      attribute :name,          ClientName
      attribute :contact_email, EmailAddress

      sets :reference
      sets :name
      sets :contact_email

      emits "ProspectAdded"
    end

    command "Engage" do
      role "COO"
      goal "Turn a prospect into a client we're actively working with"

      reference_to Client

      emits "ClientEngaged"
    end

    command "Pause" do
      role "COO"
      goal "Step back from a client without ending the relationship"

      reference_to Client

      emits "ClientPaused"
    end

    command "Reactivate" do
      role "COO"
      goal "Pick a dormant or churned relationship back up"

      reference_to Client

      emits "ClientReactivated"
    end

    command "Churn" do
      role "COO"
      goal "Mark the relationship over"

      reference_to Client

      emits "ClientChurned"
    end

    command "Revise" do
      role "COO"
      goal "Log a change to a client's own record"

      reference_to Client
      attribute :sequence, Integer
      attribute :summary,  String

      sets :revisions, append: { sequence: :sequence, summary: :summary }

      emits "ClientRevised"
    end

    query "Prospects" do
      description "The pipeline — everyone not yet a working client."
      where(status: "prospect")
      order_by :reference
    end

    query "Active" do
      description "Clients we're actively working with today."
      where(status: "active")
      order_by :reference
    end

    query "Churned" do
      description "Former clients, kept for the record."
      where(status: "churned")
      order_by :reference
    end
  end

  # THE ACTUAL PIPELINE, before pricing ever enters the room: interview
  # the client with a story workshop, write their business as a domain,
  # build a small example app on it and show them themselves modeled.
  # Only once a client has SEEN that does a Proposal go out — which is
  # why Proposal below carries a mandatory reference back to one of
  # these, the same discipline Contract already holds toward Proposal.
  aggregate "Engagement" do
    description "The technical pipeline that earns a client's trust before a Proposal ever goes out — a story workshop, a domain written from it, a demo built on that domain."

    identified_by :reference

    reference_to Client

    attribute :reference,        EngagementReference
    attribute :use_cases,        list_of(UseCase), optional: true
    attribute :domain_reference, DomainReference, optional: true
    attribute :demo_reference,   DemoReference,   optional: true
    attribute :revisions,        list_of(Revision)

    value_object "EngagementReference" do
      attribute :value, String
      invariant("an engagement is referenced") { !value.to_s.empty? }
    end

    # WHAT A STORY WORKSHOP ACTUALLY PRODUCES — not a paragraph of prose
    # someone has to re-read to find the substance, but the substance
    # itself, one use case per line, the way the interview really goes:
    # "Student should be able to see my calendar," "Admin should be able
    # to manage the arts calendar." A single WorkshopNotes blob said
    # less than this list does.
    value_object "UseCase" do
      attribute :text, String
      invariant("a use case says something") { !text.to_s.empty? }
    end

    value_object "DomainReference" do
      attribute :text, String
      invariant("a domain reference points somewhere") { !text.to_s.empty? }
    end

    value_object "DemoReference" do
      attribute :text, String
      invariant("a demo reference points somewhere") { !text.to_s.empty? }
    end

    value_object "Revision" do
      attribute :sequence, Integer
      attribute :summary,  String

      invariant("a revision is sequenced from one") { sequence.positive? }
      invariant("a revision says what changed") { !summary.to_s.empty? }
    end

    lifecycle :stage, default: "workshop_scheduled" do
      transition "CompleteWorkshop" => "workshop_completed", from: "workshop_scheduled"
      transition "DraftDomain"      => "domain_drafted",     from: "workshop_completed"
      transition "ShowDemo"         => "demo_shown",         from: "domain_drafted"
      transition "Abandon"          => "abandoned",          from: ["workshop_scheduled", "workshop_completed", "domain_drafted", "demo_shown"]
    end

    command "Schedule" do
      role "COO"
      goal "Book a story workshop with a prospective client"

      reference_to Client
      attribute :reference, EngagementReference

      sets :reference

      emits "EngagementScheduled"
    end

    command "CompleteWorkshop" do
      role "COO"
      goal "Record the use cases the story workshop surfaced"

      reference_to Engagement
      attribute :use_cases, list_of(UseCase)

      sets :use_cases

      emits "WorkshopCompleted"
    end

    command "DraftDomain" do
      role "CEO"
      goal "Write the client's business as a domain, from the workshop"

      reference_to Engagement
      attribute :domain_reference, DomainReference

      sets :domain_reference

      emits "DomainDrafted"
    end

    command "ShowDemo" do
      role "CEO"
      goal "Show the client an example app running on their own domain"

      reference_to Engagement
      attribute :demo_reference, DemoReference

      sets :demo_reference

      emits "DemoShown"
    end

    command "Abandon" do
      role "COO"
      goal "Record that a prospective engagement never turned into business"

      reference_to Engagement

      emits "EngagementAbandoned"
    end

    command "Revise" do
      role "COO"
      goal "Log a change to the engagement's own record"

      reference_to Engagement
      attribute :sequence, Integer
      attribute :summary,  String

      sets :revisions, append: { sequence: :sequence, summary: :summary }

      emits "EngagementRevised"
    end

    query "ReadyToPropose" do
      description "Demo shown — the pipeline's done its job, time to send a Proposal."
      where(stage: "demo_shown")
      order_by :reference
    end
  end

  # THE REAL SHAPE, off an actual Engagement Proposal — Overview, "What
  # you get", Term, "Out of scope", Pricing (Item / Amount / When), a
  # 30-day validity window. `LineItem`'s `cadence` is that "When" column:
  # a proposal always mixes a one-time fee with a recurring one.
  #
  # "PRESENT THE CONTRACT" IS STEP 4 OF THE REAL PIPELINE, and this is
  # what that step actually dispatches — send this Proposal, get it
  # accepted, then Contract.Draft references it below. The mandatory
  # `reference_to Engagement` is the other half of the rule: no pitch
  # goes out before a client has seen their own domain, demoed.
  aggregate "Proposal" do
    description "A pitch to a client, before there's a Contract to sign — valid for a window, then it lapses."

    identified_by :number

    reference_to Client
    reference_to Engagement

    attribute :number,       ProposalNumber
    attribute :overview,     ProposalOverview
    attribute :deliverables, list_of(Deliverable)
    attribute :term,         EngagementTerm
    attribute :exclusions,   list_of(Exclusion), optional: true
    attribute :line_items,   list_of(LineItem)
    attribute :valid_for,    ValidityWindow, optional: true
    attribute :revisions,    list_of(Revision)

    value_object "ProposalNumber" do
      attribute :value, String
      invariant("a proposal is numbered") { !value.to_s.empty? }
    end

    value_object "ProposalOverview" do
      attribute :text, String
      invariant("a proposal explains the engagement") { !text.to_s.empty? }
    end

    value_object "Deliverable" do
      attribute :text, String
      invariant("a deliverable says what you get") { !text.to_s.empty? }
    end

    value_object "EngagementTerm" do
      attribute :text, String
      invariant("a term is stated") { !text.to_s.empty? }
    end

    value_object "Exclusion" do
      attribute :text, String
      invariant("an exclusion says what's out of scope") { !text.to_s.empty? }
    end

    # "When" off the real Pricing table's third column — its own closed
    # set, the same shape banking's LedgerDirection carries, since a
    # one-time onboarding fee and a recurring membership fee are not the
    # same fact wearing different spelling.
    value_object "Cadence" do
      attribute :value, String, one_of: ["one_time", "recurring"]
    end

    # "Item / Amount / When" off the real Pricing table.
    value_object "LineItem" do
      attribute :item,     String
      attribute :cents,    Integer
      attribute :currency, String, default: "USD"
      attribute :cadence,  Cadence

      invariant("a line item is named") { !item.to_s.empty? }
      invariant("a line item bills something") { cents.positive? }
      invariant("a currency is a three-letter code") { currency.to_s.size == 3 }
    end

    value_object "ValidityWindow" do
      attribute :text, String
      invariant("a validity window is stated") { !text.to_s.empty? }
    end

    value_object "Revision" do
      attribute :sequence, Integer
      attribute :summary,  String

      invariant("a revision is sequenced from one") { sequence.positive? }
      invariant("a revision says what changed") { !summary.to_s.empty? }
    end

    lifecycle :status, default: "drafted" do
      transition "Send"     => "sent",      from: "drafted"
      transition "Accept"   => "accepted",  from: "sent"
      transition "Decline"  => "declined",  from: "sent"
      transition "Expire"   => "expired",   from: "sent"
      transition "Withdraw" => "withdrawn", from: "sent"
    end

    command "Draft" do
      role "COO"
      goal "Put a proposed engagement in writing"

      reference_to Client
      reference_to Engagement
      attribute :number,       ProposalNumber
      attribute :overview,     ProposalOverview
      attribute :deliverables, list_of(Deliverable)
      attribute :term,         EngagementTerm
      attribute :exclusions,   list_of(Exclusion), optional: true
      attribute :line_items,   list_of(LineItem)
      attribute :valid_for,    ValidityWindow, optional: true

      sets :number
      sets :overview
      sets :deliverables
      sets :term
      sets :exclusions
      sets :line_items
      sets :valid_for

      emits "ProposalDrafted"
    end

    command "Send" do
      role "COO"
      goal "Put the pitch in front of the client"

      reference_to Proposal

      emits "ProposalSent"
    end

    command "Accept" do
      role "COO"
      goal "Record that the client wants to move forward"

      reference_to Proposal

      emits "ProposalAccepted"
    end

    command "Decline" do
      role "COO"
      goal "Record that the client passed"

      reference_to Proposal

      emits "ProposalDeclined"
    end

    command "Expire" do
      role "COO"
      goal "Let a proposal lapse past its validity window"

      reference_to Proposal

      emits "ProposalExpired"
    end

    command "Withdraw" do
      role "COO"
      goal "Pull a sent proposal before the client responds"

      reference_to Proposal

      emits "ProposalWithdrawn"
    end

    command "Revise" do
      role "COO"
      goal "Log a change to a proposal before it's decided"

      reference_to Proposal
      attribute :sequence, Integer
      attribute :summary,  String

      sets :revisions, append: { sequence: :sequence, summary: :summary }

      emits "ProposalRevised"
    end

    query "Open" do
      description "Sent, awaiting a decision."
      where(status: "sent")
      order_by :number
    end

    query "Accepted" do
      description "Ready to become contracts."
      where(status: "accepted")
      order_by :number
    end
  end

  # EVERY REAL CONTRACT STARTS AS AN ACCEPTED PROPOSAL — the mandatory
  # reference below is that rule, in the type. `scope_of_work` and
  # `revisions` mirror what a real client folder actually holds:
  # contract.md alongside a tracked revision-history.md.
  aggregate "Contract" do
    description "An engagement with a client, from an accepted proposal to signature to delivery."

    identified_by :number

    reference_to Client
    reference_to Proposal

    attribute :number,        ContractNumber
    attribute :title,         ContractTitle
    attribute :value,         ContractValue
    attribute :scope_of_work, ScopeOfWork, optional: true
    attribute :revisions,     list_of(Revision)

    value_object "ContractNumber" do
      attribute :value, String
      invariant("a contract is numbered") { !value.to_s.empty? }
    end

    value_object "ContractTitle" do
      attribute :value, String
      invariant("a contract is titled") { !value.to_s.empty? }
    end

    value_object "ContractValue" do
      attribute :cents,    Integer
      attribute :currency, String, default: "USD"

      invariant("a contract is worth something") { cents.positive? }
      invariant("a currency is a three-letter code") { currency.to_s.size == 3 }
    end

    value_object "ScopeOfWork" do
      attribute :text, String
      invariant("a scope of work says what's being built") { !text.to_s.empty? }
    end

    value_object "Revision" do
      attribute :sequence, Integer
      attribute :summary,  String

      invariant("a revision is sequenced from one") { sequence.positive? }
      invariant("a revision says what changed") { !summary.to_s.empty? }
    end

    lifecycle :status, default: "drafted" do
      transition "Send"      => "sent",       from: "drafted"
      transition "Sign"      => "signed",     from: "sent"
      transition "Activate"  => "active",     from: "signed"
      transition "Complete"  => "completed",  from: "active"
      transition "Terminate" => "terminated", from: ["sent", "signed", "active"]
    end

    command "Draft" do
      role "COO"
      goal "Turn an accepted proposal into a contract to sign"

      reference_to Client
      reference_to Proposal
      attribute :number,        ContractNumber
      attribute :title,         ContractTitle
      attribute :value,         ContractValue
      attribute :scope_of_work, ScopeOfWork, optional: true

      sets :number
      sets :title
      sets :value
      sets :scope_of_work

      emits "ContractDrafted"
    end

    command "Send" do
      role "COO"
      goal "Put the draft in front of the client"

      reference_to Contract

      emits "ContractSent"
    end

    command "Sign" do
      role "COO"
      goal "Record the client's signature"

      reference_to Contract

      emits "ContractSigned"
    end

    command "Activate" do
      role "COO"
      goal "Start delivering against a signed contract"

      reference_to Contract

      emits "ContractActivated"
    end

    command "Complete" do
      role "COO"
      goal "Close out a contract we delivered in full"

      reference_to Contract

      emits "ContractCompleted"
    end

    command "Terminate" do
      role "COO"
      goal "End an engagement before it completed"

      reference_to Contract

      emits "ContractTerminated"
    end

    command "Revise" do
      role "COO"
      goal "Log a change to the contract — the same revision history a real client folder tracks"

      reference_to Contract
      attribute :sequence, Integer
      attribute :summary,  String

      sets :revisions, append: { sequence: :sequence, summary: :summary }

      emits "ContractRevised"
    end

    query "AwaitingSignature" do
      description "Sent, not yet signed — the follow-up list."
      where(status: "sent")
      order_by :number
    end

    query "Active" do
      description "Contracts we're currently delivering against."
      where(status: "active")
      order_by :number
    end

    query "Completed" do
      description "Engagements finished in full."
      where(status: "completed")
      order_by :number
    end
  end

  aggregate "Product" do
    description "Something we build to ship, carried from an idea through a vision statement to a launch."

    identified_by :codename

    attribute :codename, ProductCodename
    attribute :name,     ProductName
    attribute :vision,   VisionStatement, optional: true
    attribute :revisions, list_of(Revision)

    value_object "ProductCodename" do
      attribute :value, String
      invariant("a product has a codename") { !value.to_s.empty? }
    end

    value_object "ProductName" do
      attribute :value, String
      invariant("a product is named") { !value.to_s.empty? }
    end

    value_object "VisionStatement" do
      attribute :text, String
      invariant("a vision statement says something") { !text.to_s.empty? }
    end

    value_object "Revision" do
      attribute :sequence, Integer
      attribute :summary,  String

      invariant("a revision is sequenced from one") { sequence.positive? }
      invariant("a revision says what changed") { !summary.to_s.empty? }
    end

    lifecycle :stage, default: "concept" do
      transition "SetVision"        => "envisioned",     from: "concept"
      transition "BeginDevelopment" => "in_development", from: "envisioned"
      transition "Launch"           => "launched",        from: "in_development"
      transition "Sunset"           => "sunset",           from: "launched"
    end

    command "Conceive" do
      role "CEO"
      goal "Name a new product idea"

      attribute :codename, ProductCodename
      attribute :name,     ProductName

      sets :codename
      sets :name

      emits "ProductConceived"
    end

    command "SetVision" do
      role "CEO"
      goal "Write down what this product is for, before a line of it is built"

      reference_to Product
      attribute :vision, VisionStatement

      sets :vision

      emits "VisionSet"
    end

    command "BeginDevelopment" do
      role "CEO"
      goal "Start building against the vision"

      reference_to Product

      emits "DevelopmentStarted"
    end

    command "Launch" do
      role "CEO"
      goal "Put it in front of clients"

      reference_to Product

      emits "ProductLaunched"
    end

    command "Sunset" do
      role "CEO"
      goal "Retire a product we no longer carry"

      reference_to Product

      emits "ProductSunset"
    end

    command "Revise" do
      role "CEO"
      goal "Log a change to a product's own direction"

      reference_to Product
      attribute :sequence, Integer
      attribute :summary,  String

      sets :revisions, append: { sequence: :sequence, summary: :summary }

      emits "ProductRevised"
    end

    query "InDevelopment" do
      description "What's actively being built."
      where(stage: "in_development")
      order_by :codename
    end

    query "Launched" do
      description "What we currently ship."
      where(stage: "launched")
      order_by :codename
    end
  end

  # THE REAL SHAPE, off invoice_template.md — Invoice #, Bill to, a
  # repeatable Description/Amount line-item table, Total due. No stored
  # total : it is a sum over `line_items`, and a stored copy is a copy
  # that drifts, the same reasoning ContractValue never restates a
  # proposal's own pricing.
  aggregate "Invoice" do
    description "A bill sent to a client against a contract."

    identified_by :number

    reference_to Client
    reference_to Contract

    attribute :number,     InvoiceNumber
    attribute :due_on,     InvoiceDueDate
    attribute :line_items, list_of(LineItem)
    attribute :revisions,  list_of(Revision)

    value_object "InvoiceNumber" do
      attribute :value, String
      invariant("an invoice is numbered") { !value.to_s.empty? }
    end

    value_object "InvoiceDueDate" do
      attribute :value, String
      invariant("an invoice has a due date") { !value.to_s.empty? }
    end

    value_object "LineItem" do
      attribute :description, String
      attribute :cents,       Integer
      attribute :currency,    String, default: "USD"

      invariant("a line item is described") { !description.to_s.empty? }
      invariant("a line item bills something") { cents.positive? }
      invariant("a currency is a three-letter code") { currency.to_s.size == 3 }
    end

    value_object "Revision" do
      attribute :sequence, Integer
      attribute :summary,  String

      invariant("a revision is sequenced from one") { sequence.positive? }
      invariant("a revision says what changed") { !summary.to_s.empty? }
    end

    lifecycle :status, default: "draft" do
      transition "Send"        => "sent",     from: "draft"
      transition "MarkPaid"    => "paid",     from: "sent"
      transition "MarkOverdue" => "overdue",  from: "sent"
      transition "Void"        => "void",     from: ["draft", "sent"]
    end

    command "Draft" do
      role "CFO"
      goal "Prepare a bill for a client"

      reference_to Client
      reference_to Contract
      attribute :number,     InvoiceNumber
      attribute :due_on,     InvoiceDueDate
      attribute :line_items, list_of(LineItem)

      sets :number
      sets :due_on
      sets :line_items

      emits "InvoiceDrafted"
    end

    command "Send" do
      role "CFO"
      goal "Put the bill in front of the client"

      reference_to Invoice

      emits "InvoiceSent"
    end

    command "MarkPaid" do
      role "CFO"
      goal "Record that the client paid in full"

      reference_to Invoice

      emits "InvoicePaid"
    end

    command "MarkOverdue" do
      role "CFO"
      goal "Flag a bill that's gone past its due date unpaid"

      reference_to Invoice

      emits "InvoiceOverdue"
    end

    command "Void" do
      role "CFO"
      goal "Cancel a bill that should never have gone out"

      reference_to Invoice

      emits "InvoiceVoided"
    end

    command "Revise" do
      role "CFO"
      goal "Log a correction to a bill before it's paid"

      reference_to Invoice
      attribute :sequence, Integer
      attribute :summary,  String

      sets :revisions, append: { sequence: :sequence, summary: :summary }

      emits "InvoiceRevised"
    end

    query "Outstanding" do
      description "Sent, not yet paid — the collections list."
      where(status: "sent")
      order_by :due_on
    end

    query "Overdue" do
      description "Past due and still unpaid."
      where(status: "overdue")
      order_by :due_on
    end

    query "Paid" do
      description "Settled invoices."
      where(status: "paid")
      order_by :number
    end
  end

  # PAYMENTS AND BILLING — money a client actually sent, against an
  # invoice. A separate aggregate from Invoice on purpose : an invoice is
  # a bill, a Payment is a fact about money that moved, and a partial
  # payment (or a refund) needs to be its own record rather than a single
  # boolean the invoice flips once.
  aggregate "Payment" do
    description "Money a client sent against an invoice."

    identified_by :reference

    reference_to Invoice

    attribute :reference,   PaymentReference
    attribute :amount,      PaymentAmount
    attribute :method,      PaymentMethod
    attribute :received_on, PaymentDate

    value_object "PaymentReference" do
      attribute :value, String
      invariant("a payment is referenced") { !value.to_s.empty? }
    end

    value_object "PaymentAmount" do
      attribute :cents,    Integer
      attribute :currency, String, default: "USD"

      invariant("a payment moves something") { cents.positive? }
      invariant("a currency is a three-letter code") { currency.to_s.size == 3 }
    end

    value_object "PaymentMethod" do
      attribute :value, String
      invariant("a payment method is named") { !value.to_s.empty? }
    end

    value_object "PaymentDate" do
      attribute :value, String
      invariant("a payment has a date") { !value.to_s.empty? }
    end

    lifecycle :status, default: "recorded" do
      transition "Refund" => "refunded", from: "recorded"
    end

    command "Record" do
      role "CFO"
      goal "Log money the client actually sent"

      reference_to Invoice
      attribute :reference,   PaymentReference
      attribute :amount,      PaymentAmount
      attribute :method,      PaymentMethod
      attribute :received_on, PaymentDate

      sets :reference
      sets :amount
      sets :method
      sets :received_on

      emits "PaymentRecorded"
    end

    command "Refund" do
      role "CFO"
      goal "Give money back"

      reference_to Payment

      emits "PaymentRefunded"
    end

    query "Recorded" do
      description "Payments in hand."
      where(status: "recorded")
      order_by :received_on
    end

    query "Refunded" do
      description "Payments given back."
      where(status: "refunded")
      order_by :received_on
    end
  end

  # THE STANDING ARRANGEMENT, separate from any one Invoice — a monthly
  # membership fee is a fact about the CONTRACT, true every cycle until
  # someone pauses or cancels it, not a fact any single bill carries.
  # hecksagain has no scheduler primitive (nothing in the language fires
  # itself on a clock), so this aggregate is deliberately half of the
  # feature : it tracks WHAT is owed and WHEN it's next due, and refuses
  # to advance twice for the same cycle, but something outside the
  # domain — a cron job, a script, a person in the Founder App — still
  # has to notice `next_due_on` has arrived, call `AdvanceCycle`, and
  # draft the real Invoice. The same shape the wiring guide's
  # `DeliveryGate` port already documents for an external fact.
  aggregate "RecurringPayment" do
    description "A standing recurring charge against a contract — the monthly membership fee, still owed next cycle unless someone stops it."

    identified_by :reference

    reference_to Client
    reference_to Contract

    attribute :reference,   RecurringPaymentReference
    attribute :amount,      RecurringAmount
    attribute :cadence,     one_of("monthly", "quarterly", "annual")
    attribute :next_due_on, DueDate
    attribute :revisions,   list_of(Revision)

    value_object "RecurringPaymentReference" do
      attribute :value, String
      invariant("a recurring payment is referenced") { !value.to_s.empty? }
    end

    value_object "RecurringAmount" do
      attribute :cents,    Integer
      attribute :currency, String, default: "USD"

      invariant("a recurring payment charges something") { cents.positive? }
      invariant("a currency is a three-letter code") { currency.to_s.size == 3 }
    end

    value_object "DueDate" do
      attribute :value, String
      invariant("a due date is present") { !value.to_s.empty? }
    end

    value_object "Revision" do
      attribute :sequence, Integer
      attribute :summary,  String

      invariant("a revision is sequenced from one") { sequence.positive? }
      invariant("a revision says what changed") { !summary.to_s.empty? }
    end

    lifecycle :status, default: "active" do
      transition "Pause"  => "paused",    from: "active"
      transition "Resume" => "active",    from: "paused"
      transition "Cancel" => "cancelled", from: ["active", "paused"]
    end

    command "Start" do
      role "CFO"
      goal "Set up a standing charge for the life of a contract"

      reference_to Client
      reference_to Contract
      attribute :reference,   RecurringPaymentReference
      attribute :amount,      RecurringAmount
      attribute :cadence,     one_of("monthly", "quarterly", "annual")
      attribute :next_due_on, DueDate

      sets :reference
      sets :amount
      sets :cadence
      sets :next_due_on

      emits "RecurringPaymentStarted"
    end

    command "AdvanceCycle" do
      role "CFO"
      goal "Move the schedule to the next cycle, once this one's been billed"

      reference_to RecurringPayment
      attribute :next_due_on, DueDate

      given("only an active recurring payment advances") { status == "active" }

      sets :next_due_on

      emits "CycleAdvanced"
    end

    command "Pause" do
      role "CFO"
      goal "Stop billing without ending the arrangement"

      reference_to RecurringPayment

      emits "RecurringPaymentPaused"
    end

    command "Resume" do
      role "CFO"
      goal "Pick a paused charge back up"

      reference_to RecurringPayment

      emits "RecurringPaymentResumed"
    end

    command "Cancel" do
      role "CFO"
      goal "End the standing charge for good"

      reference_to RecurringPayment

      emits "RecurringPaymentCancelled"
    end

    command "Revise" do
      role "CFO"
      goal "Log a change to a standing charge's own terms"

      reference_to RecurringPayment
      attribute :sequence, Integer
      attribute :summary,  String

      sets :revisions, append: { sequence: :sequence, summary: :summary }

      emits "RecurringPaymentRevised"
    end

    # "Active", sorted by next_due_on — not a DueBy query with its own
    # `lte`, because next_due_on is a String (ISO dates, the same
    # convention Invoice.due_on and Payment.received_on already hold),
    # and an ordered comparator needs a number here — confirmed by the
    # seal refusing exactly that. ISO dates sort correctly as text, so
    # a caller wanting "what's due by today" reads this list and stops
    # at the first date past today rather than pushing the comparison
    # down to the query itself.
    query "Active" do
      description "Charges still billing, soonest due first."
      where(status: "active")
      order_by :next_due_on
    end
  end
end
